name: Expedition
description: On the affected player's fifteenth turn, the primary move must end on f1.
ambiguities: The single observed sample is treated as a fixed fifteenth affected-player turn and fixed f1 destination; it does not prove these are not hidden parameters.
Move counting is per affected player rather than the FIDE fullmove number.
If no ordinary legal move reaches f1, the generic no-drawback-legal-move loss applies although the observed wording does not explicitly say or lose.

name: Reflective
description: A non-pawn primary mover may land only when the horizontally reflected destination square is occupied before the move.
ambiguities: Center line means the horizontal line between ranks four and five, mapping a1 to a8; a vertical or rotational interpretation is possible.
Occupancy is evaluated in the pre-move position and either color counts.
Promotion is classified by its pawn mover and castling by the primary king destination.

name: Eye of Sauron
description: While a rook survives, non-pawn primary movers cannot advance beyond the farthest player-relative rank occupied or ordinarily reachable by an own rook.
ambiguities: Can see is interpreted as a rook's current square or an ordinary legal rook destination, not every pseudo-legal ray square.
All current rooks count, including promoted rooks; with no rook the restriction is inactive.
Pawns are exempt by the observed wording and promotion remains a pawn primary move.

name: Drag
description: The original queen moves one square at a time; if it is captured, the affected player loses.
ambiguities: Your queen means the original queen, tracked from d1 or d8; promoted queens are unrestricted and do not replace it.
A queen is a king is interpreted as one-square king geometry but not royal attacked-square restrictions.
The captured-queen loss is evaluated at the beginning of its owner's next turn and exact reconstruction requires complete history from the standard start.

name: Ooh Shiny
description: If any ordinary legal capture cannot be legally recaptured on its destination, one such capture is compulsory.
ambiguities: Recapture means an opponent standard-legal capture onto the capturing piece's destination; attacks by pinned pieces do not count.
A checking or mating capture with no legal recapture is safe.
If no safe capture exists, the restriction is inactive for that turn.
